arguments.comment: RESIDENT LOADER, load entry (JMP $F236). Call with A = file number ($00-$30, file_table $F2F9) and X/Y = load address (lo/hi). Returns carry clear and X/Y = the end address (one past the last byte), or carry set on a drive error. High Jump calls it at $0806 (stub), $08F8, $094E, $0959 and $123F (JMP); it chains files by passing the end of one as the start of the next ($0951). Uses zero page $90-$95 and $E0-$FB
Second loader entry (JMP $F26A): write a file's sectors to disk, same A and X/Y as load_file. Nothing in this snapshot calls it

load_file proper: load_setup (also sends the disk ID), then per sector: end pointer to $F1/$F2 (set_end_ptr), destination page to $EF/$F0 (set_dest_ptr), read_sector_cmd with track $94 and sector $95, wait_transfer for the 256 bytes, next_sector; the page $91 goes up by one each time until $90/$91 reaches the end $92/$93. Only the bytes before the end are stored (the drive still sends whole sectors)
save_file proper: the same sector walk as load_file_body, but each sector goes out through write_sector ($F43A) from the pages at X/Y. No caller in this snapshot

Set up a file transfer: $90/$91 = X/Y (start), $92/$93 = start + length from file_table, $94 = start track, $95 = start sector (made physical by logical_to_physical when the track's interleave is 11). Then sends drive command $0B with $45 $41 (set_disk_id_cmd), which tells the drive to expect disk ID "EA"; a disk with another ID fails its reads

Advance $94/$95 to the next sector of a file: sector = (sector + track_interleave[track]) mod sectors_per_track[track]; when that comes back to 0 every sector of the track has been used and the walk moves to the next track at sector 0, stepping over track 18 (the directory track)
A = file_table start index; returns A = index*11 mod the sector count of track Y, the physical sector that is the index-th in the interleave-11 sequence (0, 11, 1, 12, ... on a 21-sector track)

Wait until a pending reply has been received: if xfer_state is non-zero and positive, call receive_bytes until it is 0 (done) or $80 (failed, carry set). Sets the busy flag $F8 so that bg_receive does not run meanwhile; keeps X/Y ($F551/$F552)

Background receive: if no wait_transfer is running ($F8 = 0) and a reply is pending, take up to 19 bytes (count from bg_slice_bytes) and return, so a load can be spread over interrupts. No caller in this snapshot

Receive reply bytes from the drive while the countdown $F9 lasts: for each byte wait (up to $30 polls, else return) for $DD00 bit 7 to go high, then take 8 bits, each read as bit 6 of $DD00 inverted and acknowledged by a pulse on bit 5; bit 7 falling mid-byte means failure (xfer_state = $80). For command 3 and up the single byte is the whole reply. For a sector, raw mode stores each byte at ($EF/$F0) until the end pointer (end flag $E0); the other mode (not used by load_file) takes bytes 0/1 as the next track/sector link and asks for that sector itself ($F63F). After 256 bytes the transfer is done
Loop back to receive_bytes for the next byte of the sector (reached from $F62B while the in-sector count $E1 has not wrapped)
